params.body:
The owner talks to the workbench out loud, from the phone, in a stream of thought. A realtime speech model holds the conversation, Claude Code sessions in herdr do the work, and a memory keeps what was said.

## How it works

- **The conversation:** OpenAI `gpt-realtime-2.1` over WebRTC, straight from the phone's browser. It listens all the time, uses semantic turn detection so it can be interrupted, speaks back with the voice `marin`, and transcribes the owner in Dutch.
- **Its context prompt** (`PERSONA` in `bridge.mjs`) covers who it talks to and how the work runs (agents propose through the gateway, only the owner merges, Portal, mail intake). It says how to speak: short, never code, links, amounts or access codes, nothing to look at while driving. And it sets the limits: never promise that something is live, never answer an approval prompt. Each conversation also gets the projects, the running agents and the open forwarded mails.
- **Actions** (function calls, carried out by `bridge.mjs`): `start_task`, `list_agents`, `agent_update`, `tell_agent`, `list_projects`, `recall`, `remember`.
  - `start_task` opens a herdr session `voice-<n>` in workspace `voice`, with `--permission-mode auto --remote-control`, so it shows in the Claude app and pushes when it waits. Its task prompt follows `~/Projects/CLAUDE.md`, and the session ends with a `SPOKEN:` line meant to be read aloud.
  - `tell_agent` refuses an agent at an approval prompt: a misheard "yes" never grants a permission.
- **Notices:** the page asks `/changes` every 8 seconds. An agent that went from working to done or blocked is told aloud.

## Memory (`memory.mjs`)

It follows the usual split into episodic, semantic and procedural memory, with consolidation in between:

- **Episodic:** a transcript per conversation, on this machine only (`~/.local/state/voice/conversations/`), never audio. Deleted after 30 days.
- **Semantic:** the notes the agents already keep per project (`~/Projects/.memory/<project>/`), plus `~/Projects/.memory/voice/`: a journal entry per conversation and the open ideas.
- **Procedural:** `voice/preferences.md`, how the owner wants to be worked with.
- **Consolidation:** when a conversation ends (or goes quiet for ten minutes), a headless `claude -p` limited to Read, Write, Edit, Glob and Grep in `~/Projects/.memory` turns the transcript into notes. It updates an existing note rather than adding a duplicate, invents nothing, and keeps out secrets, amounts and third parties' personal data. A `remember` made during that run is not lost, and a failed run is tried again.
- **Context:** little in the window, the rest on demand. A conversation starts with the preferences, the open ideas, what was kept lately and the last three journal entries. `recall` searches the rest.

## Access

- Served on the tailnet only (`tailscale serve`), with the bridge on 127.0.0.1. Only the logins in `VOICE_LOGINS` get in (`Tailscale-User-Login`), and a POST from another origin is refused.
- The OpenAI key is sealed to the TPM (`systemd-creds`, name `openai-key`). The restricted key can mint realtime sessions and nothing else (it is refused on `/v1/models`). The phone only gets a key for one conversation.

## Checked on the workbench, on a test port with a copy of the memory

- Access: no login → 403, another login → 403, another origin → 403, the page → 200.
- `/session` mints a session with the full configuration (tools, context, transcription `gpt-live-transcribe`).
- `list_agents`, `list_projects` (40 projects), `agent_update`, `tell_agent` for an unknown agent, `remember` and `recall` all work.
- One conversation, ended, was consolidated by Claude:
  - a journal entry in Dutch;
  - the idea in `ideas.md`;
  - the stated preference in `preferences.md`;
  - the project notes left alone, since there was no new fact.

  The next session's brief carries all three.
- **Not yet tried:** the real conversation on the phone (microphone, WebRTC, voice). That needs `tailscale serve` and the phone.
params.title: Talking to the workbench: a realtime voice, sessions in herdr, and a memory
